request.system: You are an experiment designer for a fraud ranking model. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Propose 3 or 4 distinct configurations to test next with 5-fold cross-validation. Each must differ meaningfully (model family, feature set, imbalance handling or capacity). You only see cross-validation results; the test set is hidden from you. You can preview a configuration on 3 CV folds before including it in your batch. Use the preview to filter out bad configs and only propose ones that show promise. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

proposals.rationale: Best preview: PR-AUC 0.722 and precision@50 0.787, so this is the primary candidate. Calibrated probabilities without resampling suit a ranking task. The learning rate of 0.03 from the preview is not set here because the schema lets me pick it; I will keep the preview's value in the next iteration if needed.

Lower-capacity LightGBM without size features (preview 0.685, precision@50 0.767). It checks whether the model depends on volume proxies, which may reflect how the label was assigned rather than fraud. It also tests robustness of the ranking to the label's undocumented origin.
A different model family with bagging, preview 0.664 and precision@50 0.733. It is useful as a diverse, lower-variance baseline and a possible ensemble member.
Linear baseline with the lowest fold variance (sd 0.036) and a preview of 0.663. It tells us how much of the signal is linear and gives an interpretable reference for auditors.
